price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: lineup role coverage (at least one Primary Organizer, Shaper and Terminal Scorer on the floor)
structural roles defined by usage crossed with residual structural influence
within-team versus between-team variance of lineup coverage
methodological_questions: Does coverage vary enough within team-seasons across stints and lineups to be a usable within-team contrast?
Is coverage separable from lineup talent and from counts (high-usage players on court, minutes, possessions), or is it a mechanical function of them?
Does the talent control behave: stable coefficients across talent proxies, no collinearity blow-up, no outcome leakage, no look-ahead?
Are role labels reliable, and are they computed from the same possessions that are later used to score the lineup?
Is there enough possession exposure per lineup or stint?

historical_evidence.finding: Cross-possession play-type memory failed its decay-sanity gate. Flat lifts collapsed under a within-team baseline and were attributed to a team-quality confound (limited by confounding).

Audit of inferred play-type labels failed overall: OTHER was 20.2% against a target below 10%, 40.8% of labels were low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw rate was far below benchmark, and MIA identity checks failed. The record says labels have systematic issues (verdict tool_eval_fail).
Star-suppression lineup cells (n of at least 30) were reported with no placebo or matching. Later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts (risk: placebo dependence).
Per-star next-possession suppression cells had n_after of 32-95 against thousands of baseline possessions, with no multiplicity correction.

Teammate profile similarity did not separate absorption from cascade (wrong-signed Spearman -0.19). The failure type is recorded as a powered null, and similar-profile teammates were almost always findable.
Counter rankings were unstable across levels where cells were small (n_mu as low as 5). Risks recorded: mechanical floor and sample size.
Inferred defensive-scheme labels could not separate real adjustment from noise, and transition matrices were near-uniform, consistent with label noise.
Observed on-ball scheme labels were available for only 14.9% and 3.3% of possessions (failed gate).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pooled possession-level effects without a within-team baseline
failed_approaches.why: Apparent effects were produced by team-quality confounding (mechanism recorded as artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using rule-based inferred play-type labels at face value
failed_approaches.why: Label classification error and leakage of foul possessions into OTHER, which undermines downstream findings.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reporting named-star or lineup cells without placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: No placebo; mechanism unclear; later work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Many small per-player cells with no multiplicity correction
Ranking at fine granularity (matchup level) from sparse cells
failed_approaches.why: Small samples and a mechanical floor, so the rankings were inconclusive.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests lineup role coverage directly.
The project has recorded that pooled effects can be team-quality artifacts and that within-team baselines are needed (FAM:SF-CHT-029).
The project has recorded that its inferred play-type and initiator labels failed a label audit (FAM:SF-APPM-014). Role labels built from them inherit this risk.
The project has recorded repeated failures from sparse cells, missing multiplicity control and missing placebos (FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPM-055).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether lineup coverage varies within teams, or how much.
Whether coverage is separable from talent, usage counts or minutes.
How a talent control behaves (stability, collinearity, leakage).
Whether the Structural Influence role categories are reliable at lineup level.
Any outcome relationship of coverage, which this question does not need to address.
own_inferences: The glossary defines roles by crossing usage (above or below the rotation median) with residual influence beyond usage. Coverage is therefore partly a mechanical function of how many high-usage players are on court, so separability from 'counts' faces a mechanical-floor risk. Residualizing on count-of-high-usage-players may remove most of the variance.

Role labels and lineup possession mixes come from the same possession records. If the lineup coverage measure and any outcome or talent measure share possessions, circularity and leakage are possible. Role assignments should be computed on data disjoint from the lineup-level analysis (for example from other games or the other half-season).
Talent control would likely rely on box-score or plus-minus proxies. Plus-minus proxies are outcome-derived and correlate with usage, so a talent control could be collinear with the role definitions.

With about 4,700 possessions per team-season, five-man units are sparse. Within-team variation estimated from raw lineups will mix real variation with sampling noise, so a reliability correction is needed.

Because coverage depends on the roster, much of the variation may be between-team, or between player-availability states. The 'within team' claim needs a variance decomposition rather than an assertion.
The question has three sub-claims. It can only be called supported if all three hold, so the joint probability is lower than for any single one.
Role labels from the 2025-26 data are unaffected by outcomes. The partial 2025-26 data before 2026-06-21 should not be mixed with the complete seasons.
uncertainties: The exact operational definitions of 'coverage', 'separable' and 'behaves' are not given. This design fixes them in advance.
I did not retrieve the data catalog, so I do not know whether on-court lineup identifiers or a clean talent metric are available.
No retrieved record shows reliability of the role labels at season, half-season or lineup level.
Whether other project records (not returned) address lineup coverage is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: No retrieved record answers the question, so the evidence did not change the topic. It did change the design. The recorded artifacts, label failures and sparse-cell failures led me to choose proceed_with_changes rather than proceed. The changes are within-team baselines, disjoint-sample role assignment, a label reliability gate, shuffle and placebo checks, minimum exposure thresholds, and multiplicity control.

blocking_constraints.text: Coverage is partly determined by the count of high-usage players on court because roles are median-split on usage. Separability from counts may be impossible by construction.
Five-man units have few possessions each. Most lineups will fall below any reasonable exposure threshold, so analysis must use stints or players-on-floor aggregates with minimum-possession gates.
Role labels derive from inferred play-type labels that failed an audit (FAM:SF-APPM-014).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tested lineup coverage. The related records provide methodological warnings only: team-quality confounding, label error, sparse cells, missing multiplicity control and missing placebos.

risks.text: Coverage follows from the number of high-usage players on court by construction of the usage median split. 'Separable from counts' needs a null from random or permuted lineup composition.
Team quality and roster composition drive both coverage and talent. A within-team design is needed (FAM:SF-CHT-029).
A talent control built from plus-minus or net-rating metrics is outcome-derived and can absorb the effect or create collinearity.
Roles estimated from the same season and games as the lineups scored would leak. Look-ahead is possible if season-level roles are applied to early-season lineups.
Play-type and initiator labels failed a prior audit (FAM:SF-APPM-014). Role labels may be noisy or biased by team.
Role labels near the usage median or at zero residual influence will flip between samples. Lineup coverage then varies from classification noise rather than real structure.
Most five-man units have too few possessions. Estimated within-team variance will be inflated by sampling noise unless corrected.
There are 90 team-seasons. Team-level random effects and talent-by-team interactions may be underpowered.
Several talent proxies, coverage definitions and season splits would multiply the number of comparisons.
Rosters and injuries change within a season, so season-level roles may not apply to later lineups. The 2025-26 data are also partly incomplete at different dates.
Without a shuffled-composition placebo, any observed 'variation' cannot be distinguished from the mechanical variation implied by random rosters (FAM:SF-CHT-009).

design.estimand: (1) Share of variance in a stint-level coverage indicator (at least one Organizer, one Shaper, one Terminal on court) lying within team-season, versus between team-seasons, after reliability correction. (2) The partial association of coverage with a pre-specified talent measure and with the count of high-usage players on court, with the residual coverage variance after removing both. (3) The talent-control behaviour: stability of the coverage-to-talent coefficient across at least two talent proxies, the variance inflation factor, and agreement of the sign.
design.unit: Stint (same ten players on court) within team-season, weighted by possessions. A lineup-level summary is secondary.
design.sample: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season plus playoffs as the primary sample, with 2025-26 complete regular season as a held-out replication. Exclude garbage time. Stints with fewer than a pre-fixed minimum of possessions (for example 20) are dropped. Playoffs are analysed separately. 2025-26 playoffs are excluded from the primary analysis, and partial 2025-26 data are not mixed in.
design.power: 90 team-seasons and 420,993 possessions are available. The number of stints above the exposure gate is unknown and must be counted before analysis. A pre-analysis check requires at least 30 stints per team-season above the gate for most team-seasons, otherwise switch to a half-season split with player-level aggregates. A minimum detectable within-team variance share should be set from the stint count and reported before testing.
design.controls: Assign roles using data disjoint from the scored stints (for example roles from odd-numbered games, coverage from even-numbered games, then swap). Control for count of high-usage players on court, minutes and possessions, and a talent measure that is not derived from the same possessions (for example prior-season box-score metrics). Use team-season fixed effects for within-team estimates. Report results with and without the usage-count control to expose the mechanical floor.
design.falsification: Permutation placebo: within team-season, shuffle player-to-role assignments among rotation players and shuffle stint compositions, then recompute coverage variance and separability. The claim is rejected if observed within-team variance does not exceed the null, or if coverage residual on counts and talent is no more than the permuted residual. Role reliability gate: split-half agreement of role labels must meet a pre-set threshold (for example Cohen kappa of at least 0.6), otherwise the study stops as untestable. Also run a label-error sensitivity analysis using only high-confidence play-type possessions (FAM:SF-APPM-014).
design.multiplicity: One primary estimand per sub-claim (three in total) with Holm correction. Talent proxies and coverage definitions are fixed in advance, and anything else is labelled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if all three hold: (a) within-team share of coverage variance exceeds the permutation null and a pre-set floor after reliability correction; (b) residual coverage variance after removing counts and talent exceeds the permutation null by a pre-set margin and is stable across replication seasons; (c) talent-control coefficients keep the same sign across proxies with VIF below 5, and results replicate in the 2025-26 holdout. Rejected if (a) or (b) fails with adequate power. Untestable if the role reliability gate or the exposure check fails. Artifact if separability disappears when counts are controlled or when roles are assigned on disjoint data.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 as available on 2026-07-13, with the derived play-type possession graph as built on that date. Freeze the dataset hash, the classifier version and the role-definition rules before analysis.

research_concepts: role classification from play-type possession records
methodological_questions: Is lineup role coverage separable from talent and possession counts?
Does coverage vary within team-seasons enough to test?
How does talent control behave (stability, collinearity, leakage) when adjusting coverage effects?
How reliable are derived role labels and are they outcome-derived?
What sample size and exposure per lineup are needed?
args.query: lineup coverage of organizer shaper terminal roles within-team variation separable from talent and counts, talent control behavior

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

TOOL_RESULT glossary:
# Terminology used in the research questions

This glossary is given identically in every condition. It defines terms only and reports no results. Definitions follow the published papers (Structural Influence; Detecting Defensive Suppression) where they exist.

- **Possession, PPP:** a team's continuous spell with the ball; PPP is points per possession.
- **H1, H2:** first half (periods 1 and 2) and second half (periods 3 and 4) of a game. RS and PO: regular season and playoffs.
- **Play type:** the label assigned to each possession by the project's rule-based classifier from play-by-play events. Labels include PNR (pick-and-roll ball handler), DRIVE, CUT, SPOT_UP, PULL_UP, POST_UP, PUTBACK and TRANSITION. A play-type mix is a team's share of possessions in each play type.
- **Initiator, initiation:** the offensive player whose action starts the possession's play type (for example the cutter on a cut, the ball handler on a pick-and-roll). Initiation records are possession-level rows linking initiator, play type and points.
- **Inferrer:** the classifier step that infers a play type (for example a pick-and-roll) from play-by-play text when it is not recorded directly.
- **Suppression trigger:** a team, play type and game in which the team's PPP on that play type falls sharply from H1 to H2 under fixed minimum-attempt rules; read as the defense possibly taking the action away.
- **Continuation, counter:** after a trigger, continuation means the offense keeps running the triggered play type; a counter is a different play type run instead.
- **BEST, AVOID (counter tiers):** the strategy app's matchup-ranked counter recommendations after a trigger. BEST is the top-ranked counter play type for that matchup, AVOID the lowest-ranked.
- **Structural fingerprint:** a team's standardized pattern of how play types share initiators.
- **Structural influence (load, L):** how much a team's structural fingerprint changes when one player's initiations are removed. L_pre is that quantity measured from games before an absence.
- **Usage:** a player's share of team possessions he initiates or finishes.
- **Role categories (Structural Influence paper):** by crossing usage (above or below the rotation median) with residual influence (structural influence beyond what usage predicts): Primary Organizer (high usage, positive residual), Shaper (low usage, positive residual), Terminal Scorer (high usage, residual at or below zero), Role Occupant or Specialist (low usage, residual at or below zero).
- **Connector:** a structural-role label used in later studies for players whose presence links teammates' play types; the exact rule varied between studies.
- **Hub:** a high-structural-influence player around whom a team's initiations are organized.
- **Absence spell:** a run of consecutive games a player misses (the main studies used at least 15).
- **Displacement (D_real):** how far teammates' play-type mix moves during an absence spell relative to before it (one minus the cosine similarity of the two mixes).
- **Mover, decoy:** a mover is a player who changed teams between seasons; decoys are comparison players used as placebo matches for a mover.
- **Stint:** an interval of play with the same ten players on the court.
- **Garbage time:** late-game possessions with a lopsided score, usually excluded.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm checking whether the role definitions are circular, since they're built from usage and residual influence, which in turn rely on the same possession data used for the lineup coverage measure. I'm also noting that the season-level role includes lineup possessions. I'll skip any extra tool call and move toward writing the final answer.

I'm now treating the question as a measurement-validity check rather than an outcome question, with three parts to test: whether lineup coverage varies within a team, whether it can be separated from talent and from counts of high-usage players, and whether talent control holds up. I'd check variation with a variance decomposition, separability with partial correlations or VIFs, and talent control with a stability check across proxies and a permuted-label placebo. The main risk is mechanical: with five players on the floor, role definitions from median splits fix how many high-usage players are present, so coverage is partly determined by roster composition.

I'm sizing the lineup data next: around 420,993 possessions across 90 team-seasons, which works out to roughly 4,700 per team-season, but spread over many five-man lineups, most with only a few possessions each. That sparsity will limit how reliably coverage can be estimated. I'm leaning toward proceeding with changes to the design, since the question is testable even if the outcomes are uncertain.
